provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: The power of words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state kind words.
The pupils should be able to explain how words affect others.

Introduction:
We use words every day. Words can make people happy or sad.

Content:
Words are like magic. Kind words build people. Bad words break people. When you say thank you, you build someone. When you shout, you break someone.

Class activity:
Let's make a kindness chain. Each child says one kind word to the next child.

Evaluation questions:
What kind words do you know?
How do bad words make people feel?
What should you say when someone helps you?

Summary:
Words are powerful. Use kind words always.

topics.title: Self discipline
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify disciplined actions.
The pupils should be able to explain why discipline is important.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about words. Today we learn about self discipline.

Content:
Self discipline means doing what is right even when no one is watching. It means waiting for your turn. It means following rules in class.

Class activity:
Let's play the freeze game. When the teacher says freeze, everyone must stop moving.

Evaluation questions:
What is self discipline?
Give an example of discipline in class.
Why is discipline important?

Summary:
Discipline helps us do the right thing always.

topics.title: Accountability
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define accountability.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to apologize.

Introduction:
Sometimes we make mistakes. Today we learn about taking responsibility for our actions.

Content:
Accountability means owning what you do. If you break something, say sorry. If you hurt someone, make it better. Being honest shows you are accountable.

Class activity:
Let's practice saying sorry to a friend. We will shake hands after saying sorry.

Evaluation questions:
What does accountability mean?
What should you say when you make a mistake?
How can you fix a mistake?

Summary:
Accountability means taking responsibility for your actions.

topics.title: Generosity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define generosity.
The pupils should be able to list generous actions.

Introduction:
We have learned about being responsible. Today we learn about giving to others.

Content:
Generosity means sharing what you have. It could be your toys or your food. When you share, you make others happy. Being generous makes you feel good too.

Class activity:
We will bring something small to share with the class next week.

Evaluation questions:
What is generosity?
Name something you can share with others.
How does sharing make you feel?

Summary:
Generosity is sharing what you have with others.

topics.title: Mercy wins
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain mercy.
The pupils should be able to show mercy in a pretend situation.

Introduction:
When we argue with friends, we need to be kind. Today we learn about showing mercy.

Content:
Mercy means forgiving others even when they wrong you. It means not being angry for too long. Mercy helps us make peace with friends.

Class activity:
Let's make a peace pact. We will shake hands and say sorry to each other.

Evaluation questions:
What is mercy?
Why is mercy important in friendships?
How can you show mercy to a friend?

Summary:
Mercy means forgiving others and making peace.

topics.title: Courage to stand
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define courage.
The pupils should be able to identify brave actions.

Introduction:
Sometimes we need to be brave even when scared. Today we learn about courage.

Content:
Courage means standing up for what is right even when others disagree. It means telling the truth even when afraid. Being brave helps us do good things.

Class activity:
Let's act out brave stories. We will pretend to stand up for a friend.

Evaluation questions:
What is courage?
Name something brave you can do.
Why is courage important?

Summary:
Courage means being brave and standing up for what is right.

topics.title: Humility
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to define humility.
The pupils should be able to show humility in an activity.

Introduction:
Being great is good, but being humble is better. Today we learn about humility.

Content:
Humility means not being proud or boastful. It means helping others without showing off. A humble person serves others quietly.

Class activity:
Let's secretly help a friend today. We will do something nice without telling others.

Evaluation questions:
What is humility?
How can you show humility at school?
Why is humility important?

Summary:
Humility means being great but serving others quietly.

topics.title: Faithful in little
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain faithfulness.
The pupils should be able to complete small tasks faithfully.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about humility. Today we learn about being faithful in small things.

Content:
Faithfulness means doing your best in small tasks. It means finishing what you start. When you are faithful in little things, people trust you with bigger things.

Class activity:
Each child will take care of a plant for one week. We will see who is most faithful.

Evaluation questions:
What is faithfulness?
Why is it important to be faithful in small things?
Give an example of being faithful at home.

Summary:
Being faithful in small tasks builds trust for bigger ones.

topics.title: Nation building
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify ways to build Nigeria.
The pupils should be able to make a nation promise.

Introduction:
We are part of Nigeria. Today we learn how we can help build our nation.

Content:
Building Nigeria means doing good things in our country. It means keeping our environment clean. It means following rules and helping others.

Class activity:
We will draw pictures of how we can build Nigeria.

Evaluation questions:
What does nation building mean?
Name one way to build Nigeria.
Why is it important to love our country?

Summary:
We can all help build Nigeria by doing good things.

topics.title: Revision and values day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall all values learned.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate one value.

Introduction:
Today we remember all the good values we learned this term.

Content:
We have learned about words, discipline, accountability, generosity, mercy, courage, humility, faithfulness and nation building. These values help us become good children.

Class activity:
Each child will show one value they learned. We will give medals to everyone.

Evaluation questions:
Name one value you learned this term.
Which value is your favorite and why?
How can you use these values at home?

Summary:
All these values help us become better children.
